cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Who Changed It?
cards.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. I can't open the cupboard. Was the sofa this close yesterday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's more room for yoga now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Did making that room involve moving the sofa?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, I moved it. I put the things you'll need somewhere easier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How thoughtful. Would those be the mugs in your sock drawer, or has someone else improved the kitchen too?

mechanism: A interprets physical rearrangement as a pupil applying its lessons and asks progressively specific questions until B admits responsibility.
confusable: The teaching praise is a way to elicit ownership, not merely approving a redesigned space.
comparison: Personal writing clue versus practical spatial changes and missing mugs.
seedUse: Keep D40 sofa/cupboard/yoga/mugs; S05 taught clear-space method supplies the reason to grade what B did while asking who changed it.
